summary: LLM inference costs are driven by token volume, model tier selection, and infrastructure utilization, and most teams overspend 2-5x more than necessary. Stacking five to six optimization levers—prompt caching, model routing, semantic caching, batching, token compression, and output constraints—reliably delivers 60-80% total cost reduction without measurable quality loss. A real-world reputation SaaS cut its bill 79% (from $41.60 to $8.90 per 1,000 replies) by layering these techniques.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching
techniques.description: Reuse previously processed input tokens (system prompts, large context, few-shot examples) server-side so repeated prefixes aren't reprocessed and re-billed at full rate. Providers charge heavily discounted rates for cache hits.
techniques.savings: 50-90% on cached input tokens (PwC: 41-80% total API cost reduction across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google)
techniques.example: On Anthropic, mark a stable 2,048+ token system prompt with cache_control; subsequent calls within the cache window pay only 10% of normal input price for that prefix.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Cache responses keyed by the semantic meaning of requests (via embeddings) rather than exact string match, so paraphrased or similar queries return cached answers without an API call.
techniques.savings: Up to 73% cost reduction; typical 45% cache hit rate
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or Redis semantic cache to embed incoming queries and return a stored answer when cosine similarity to a prior query exceeds 0.95, skipping the LLM entirely.

techniques.name: Model Routing / Right-Sizing the Model
techniques.description: Route each request to the cheapest model that can handle it—classification/extraction to budget tiers, complex reasoning to flagship models—instead of sending everything to the most expensive model.
techniques.example: Send 70% of traffic to GPT-4o-mini/Haiku 4.5 and reserve GPT-4o/Opus for the 5% of queries flagged as high-complexity, cutting blended cost per call sharply.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Trim system prompts, remove filler phrases, replace verbose few-shot blocks with a single clear example, and compress context using tools like LLMLingua before sending to the API.
techniques.example: Cut a bloated 600-token system prompt down to under 200 tokens by removing redundant instructions and politeness filler, dropping input cost ~30% on every call.

techniques.name: Output Constraints (max_tokens + structured output)
techniques.description: Cap max_tokens and use structured output schemas / JSON mode instead of verbose free-form responses, since output tokens cost 4-5x more than input tokens on flagship models.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and request a JSON schema with only the needed fields so the model can't produce a runaway, chatty answer that's billed at $10-15 per million tokens.

techniques.name: Batch Processing (Batch API)
techniques.description: Submit non-latency-sensitive requests through async batch endpoints that process within a window (e.g. 24h) in exchange for a steep discount.
techniques.savings: 50% off (OpenAI/Anthropic batch); up to 95% when combined with prompt caching
techniques.example: Run nightly bulk summarization of the day's support tickets via Anthropic's Batch API to pay half price with no code changes beyond the endpoint.

techniques.name: Continuous Batching & KV Cache Reuse (self-hosted)
techniques.description: At the serving/runtime layer, use continuous batching, PagedAttention, and KV cache reuse (via vLLM/TGI) to pack more requests per GPU and avoid recomputing shared prefixes.
techniques.example: Serve Llama 3 with vLLM's continuous batching so dozens of concurrent requests share GPU cycles instead of running one-at-a-time, roughly doubling effective throughput.

techniques.name: Quantization & Model Distillation (self-hosted)
techniques.description: Reduce model footprint with INT8/INT4 quantization or distill a smaller model, lowering GPU memory and cost while keeping acceptable quality for most tasks.
techniques.example: Run a 4-bit (AWQ/GPTQ) quantized Llama 3 70B to fit on a single smaller GPU instead of two, cutting serving cost materially.

techniques.name: GPU Right-Sizing / Fixing Under-Provisioning (self-hosted)
techniques.description: Match GPU resource requests to actual peak usage instead of over-provisioning; the biggest hidden inference cost is GPUs billed at 100% while running at ~8% utilization.
techniques.savings: Large—reclaim the gap between requested and used GPU capacity
techniques.example: Per Cast AI's 2026 report, a workload using 9GB requested an H100 80GB at 8% utilization—right-size the request or bin-pack multiple workloads onto one GPU.

techniques.name: Multi-Tier Caching (exact + semantic + session)
techniques.description: Combine exact-match caching, semantic caching, and session/context management in layers so each request is resolved at the cheapest possible tier before hitting the model.
techniques.savings: Compounds with other levers toward 70-85% total reduction
techniques.example: Check an exact-match Redis key first, fall back to semantic similarity search, then reuse cached session context—only calling the LLM on a full miss.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic cache layer for LLM apps that stores and retrieves responses by embedding similarity, reducing repeat API calls and latency.

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK that gives a single OpenAI-compatible API across 100+ providers with built-in model routing, caching, rate limiting, and cost tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; LiteLLM Enterprise from ~$250/month for SSO, support, and advanced features

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform providing request logging, cost analytics, caching, and prompt management via a one-line proxy.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); paid plans from ~$20/month plus usage-based tiers

tools.name: Redis (Semantic Cache / LangCache)
tools.description: In-memory data store with vector search used for exact-match and semantic caching of LLM responses to cut tokens and improve latency.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; Redis Cloud from ~$5/month, enterprise/managed tiers higher

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in caching (in-memory, SQLite, Redis, semantic), model abstraction, and routing primitives for building optimized pipelines.

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft prompt-compression library that shrinks prompts (including long context and few-shot examples) by up to 20x while preserving task performance.

tools.name: vLLM
tools.description: High-throughput open-source inference/serving engine using PagedAttention and continuous batching to maximize GPU utilization for self-hosted models.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API marketplace routing requests across many model providers with automatic fallback, price comparison, and provider-level cost optimization.
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-as-you-go pass-through pricing with a small routing margin; no base fee

tools.name: Cast AI
tools.description: Kubernetes automation platform that right-sizes and bin-packs GPU workloads to eliminate over-provisioning and cut self-hosted inference infrastructure cost.
tools.pricing_paid: Free cost-visibility tier; automation pricing based on managed spend/savings share

quick_wins: Enable prompt caching on your stable system prompt and large context (50-90% off cached input tokens, near-zero code change).
Set max_tokens and switch to structured/JSON output to cut output tokens ~50%—output costs 4-5x input on flagship models.
Route cheap tasks (classification, extraction, summarization) to a budget tier like GPT-4o-mini or Haiku 4.5 instead of a flagship model (40-70% savings).
Trim system prompts to under 200 tokens by removing filler and collapsing few-shot examples to a single example (~30% input savings).
Add a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) to serve repeat/paraphrased queries without an API call (~45% hit rate, up to 73% savings).
